title: Client keepalive probe leak causes proxy SSL race leading to tenant 5xx waves
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a high-throughput migration for a single enterprise tenant we saw recurring 5xx spikes and long-tail timeouts on the Hosted API. Initial signs looked like normal retry amplification, but the root cause was a subtle interaction between client-side TCP/HTTP keepalive probes (sent by the customer's SDK with aggressive defaults), our edge proxy's TLS session handling, and a race in the backend connection handoff. The aggressive probes created a flood of short-lived connection churn; the proxy attempted SSL session renegotiation/cleanup for those connections and occasionally returned 502/504 during in-flight requests. Those transient 5xx responses triggered customer and SDK retries which amplified load, causing KV-cache churn and backend queue pressure.
comments: 2025-02-18 08:55 UTC - Customer A reported intermittent 5xxs during large streaming ingest; reported latency and error rate increase in US-WEST region.
2025-02-18 09:10 UTC - Oncall acknowledged incident and created this ticket; Pager duty bridge opened. Initial mitigation: raise circuit-breaker threshold for the tenant to reduce retries.

2025-02-18 10:20 UTC - Observability: Grafana showed spike in edge connection churn, TLS handshake latency, and backend request queue length. SRE confirmed correlation between client SYN bursts and 502s.
2025-02-18 11:05 UTC - Reproduced locally by running customer's SDK with default keepalive interval (3s) at scale; observed large numbers of ephemeral connections and socket churn.
2025-02-18 13:00 UTC - Hotpatch v1 deployed to edge: special-casing incoming probe responses to avoid triggering backend TLS renegotiation. Temporary rate-limit at proxy ingress applied per-tenant.
2025-02-18 15:30 UTC - Customer comms: updated customer with mitigation steps and requested they temporarily increase client keepalive interval to 60s as a conservative safe default.

2025-02-19 09:00 UTC - Hotfix v2 deployed to runtime-1.22: backend now defers KV-cache eviction on mid-handshake errors, adds handshake backoff, and reduces aggressive retrying inside the runtime for transient 5xxs.
2025-02-20 12:45 UTC - SDK team released patched client 2.3.1 with a safer default keepalive and socket reuse improvements; added telemetry to surface aggressive keepalive usage.
2025-02-21 10:10 UTC - Incident declared resolved after 48 hours of stable metrics and no recurrence for the impacted tenant. Postmortem compiled and shared.
2025-02-21 11:00 UTC - PM review completed; customer satisfaction update drafted and CS forwarded to account team.
2025-02-21 15:00 UTC - Design review scheduled for long-term connection management changes.
resolution: Applied a two-stage fix: (1) edge-level mitigation to sheath aggressive keepalive probes and per-tenant ingress rate-limiting, (2) runtime hotfix to make TLS handshake failures non-evicting for KV cache and to add conservative retry suppression. SDK defaults were hardened and a client release pushed. Monitoring and alerts updated to surface probe-driven churn.
follow_up_actions: Implement permanent edge proxy change to classify and handle probe traffic without triggering backend TLS renegotiation (owner: Edge team, due 2025-03-05)
Roll out SDK telemetry to detect aggressive keepalive patterns across tenants and auto-contact customers (owner: SDK team, due 2025-03-12)
Add automated chaos tests that simulate aggressive client probe rates to prevent regressions (owner: Reliability, due 2025-04-01)
Review and document retry policy defaults across SDKs/Runtime/Edge to ensure consistent jitter and idempotency guarantees (owner: Platform, Cycle 45)
Update customer playbook with explicit guidance for keepalive/connection settings for high-throughput streaming use-cases (owner: Solutions, due 2025-03-01)
